text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. Welcome to your consultation; as a newborn, I will be asking you questions about your health to understand your condition. Can you tell me how many days old your baby is and describe any symptoms you have noticed?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the history. I note this is a term female newborn with no prenatal care and unknown immunization status. Have you noticed any jaundice, poor feeding, or signs of respiratory distress in the baby?

REQUEST TEST: Blood_Type_and_Coombs, G6PD_assay, CBC_with_Differential.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome.

The clinical triad of continuous heart murmur (PDA), bluish non-blanching macules (blueberry muffin rash), and cataracts (cloudy lenses), combined with sensorineural hearing loss, is pathognomonic for congenital rubella.
